jobs.description:
Job Purpose

The New York Stock Exchange (an Intercontinental Exchange company) is growing its Information Technology Compliance (ITC) team, and we’re looking for an IT Compliance Analyst to help build what comes next. ITC owns the development, implementation, and management of NYSE’s risk-based IT compliance program, keeping our exchange technology aligned with Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) regulation, industry standards, and internal policy.

You’ll work directly with regulators, senior technologists, and business leaders across NYSE and ICE, gaining a front-row view into how a top-tier exchange operates. You’ll gain the rare opportunity to learn advanced exchange technology concepts and bring your own judgment and problem-solving to take ownership in a fast-moving regulatory environment, where the details really matter.

Responsibilities

Support efforts responding to external regulatory examinations and requests of NYSE’s IT systems, policies, and processes, often working across multiple business units under tight deadlines.
Own activities that keep NYSE compliant with SEC Regulation Systems Compliance and Integrity (Reg SCI) and similar frameworks, adhering to strict reporting deadlines.
Act as a connective thread between business, technology, regulatory, and legal teams to keep compliance objectives moving.
Advise stakeholders on IT compliance topics that are often technically complex, translating between disciplines.
Keep leadership informed through ongoing monitoring and reporting of compliance status.
Dig into technical assessments of new systems, system changes, and software defects, spotting regulatory, operational, and functional risk and proposing compensating controls.

Knowledge And Experience

3+ years of experience in one or more of:
IT Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC)
IT SDLC or business analysis
IT audit or controls assurance
Government or industry regulator role focused on technology compliance
Equities and options markets, automated trading, or low-latency market data
Regulatory compliance more broadly, ideally in financial services and/or fintech

Relevant certifications a plus (ISACA, ISC², ITIL, etc.).
Solid grounding in IT risk and control frameworks (COBIT, ISO, NIST, ITIL) and the ability to apply them to real exchange systems.
Comfort reading and interpreting financial securities regulation.
A self-starter: you’re energized by ambiguity, not stalled by it, and you bring good judgment and instinct to unfamiliar problems, proactively flagging what needs a closer look.
Reliable follow-through: you take direction and run with it while knowing when to self-solve or escalate, never working on assumptions.
Quick to learn: you often get it the first time, ask when you don’t, and move on to what’s next.
Flexibility to be available outside traditional business hours when markets or regulatory deadlines demand it.
Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the versatility to explain complex technical topics to very different audiences.
Interest in bringing automation to compliance workflows and data analysis (Python, AI tools, etc.). Experience is great, but willingness to learn is essential.

New York Base Salary Range

The expected base salary for this role, if located in New York, is between $100,000 - 130,000 USD.  The base salary range does not include Intercontinental Exchange’s incentive compensation.  While we provide this range as general guidance, at ICE we compensate employees based on the skillset and experience of the individual. Regular full-time ICE employees are eligible for a suite of competitive employee benefits, including healthcare coverage (medical, dental and vision), a 401(k) plan, life insurance, time off, and paid leave for qualifying circumstances.

Illinois Base Salary Range

The expected base salary for this role, if located in Illinois, is between $80,000 - 100,000 USD.  The base salary range does not include Intercontinental Exchange’s incentive compensation.  While we provide this range as general guidance, at ICE we compensate employees based on the skillset and experience of the individual. Regular full-time ICE employees are eligible for a suite of competitive employee benefits, including healthcare coverage (medical, dental and vision), a 401(k) plan, life insurance, time off, and paid leave for qualifying circumstances.

Review site constraints and opportunities

Work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams
Prepare planning applications and supporting statements

An undergraduate or bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in a relevant discipline, such as Urban Planning, Geography, Urban Design or a related planning subject.

Required for this role, Understanding of the UK planning system (TCPA, DCO, Local Plans, NPPF); strong report writing; critical thinker/ problem solver; policy interpretation; research and evidence assessment; stakeholder engagement; presentation skills; consultation analysis; consultation monitoring and responses; time management and managing multiple workstreams; team collaboration; familiar with key software packages (e.g. strong skills in MS Excel, Word, PowerPoint, SharePoint, MS Teams, Copilot, etc)

Desirable skills the above but with greater depth/ competency plus basic to intermediate GIS skills; appreciation of development viability, programme and risk considerations and client-focussed thinking; interest in regeneration, policy, and infrastructure

new_jobs.description:
We are looking for an Infrastructure Planning Leader to own Meta's medium-range and long-range infrastructure capacity planning process end to end. In this role you will work across infrastructure engineering teams, product groups, and finance to translate product and AI roadmaps into a multi-year plan for compute, power, and data center capacity. You will design the planning process itself, build alignment on it across a large and technically diverse set of partner teams, educate those teams on how to participate, and guide both demand and supply organizations through its execution. This is a senior individual contributor role for a planning practitioner with depth across data center infrastructure, power, supply chain, and infrastructure demand.

Infrastructure Planning Lead Responsibilities:

Own the medium-range and long-range infrastructure capacity planning processes end to end, from demand collection through supply commitment.
Partner with infrastructure engineering teams, product groups, and finance to translate product and AI roadmaps into multi-year compute, power, and data center capacity requirements.
Design, document, and iterate on the planning process, including the planning calendar, required inputs, decision checkpoints, and published outputs.
Educate partner teams on the planning process and build the shared definitions, artifacts, and templates that teams use to participate in it.
Guide demand teams in forecasting and articulating their infrastructure requirements, and guide supply teams in translating those requirements into build, procurement, and deployment plans.
Identify gaps between forecasted infrastructure demand and planned supply, and drive the trade-off decisions needed to close them.
Define the metrics used to measure forecast accuracy, plan attainment, and capacity utilization, and drive improvement against those metrics over time.
Partner with data center and supply chain teams on lead times, constraints, and sequencing that determine when capacity can be delivered.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience
15+ years of experience in capacity planning, supply chain planning, or demand planning
Experience designing and owning a recurring, multi-quarter planning process spanning multiple organizations
Experience with data center infrastructure planning, including power, capacity, or supply chain constraints
Experience presenting planning recommendations and trade-offs to executive-level audiences

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience with long-range capacity planning for hyperscale, cloud, or large-scale data center infrastructure
Experience with capacity planning for AI or machine learning training and inference workloads
Experience with quantitative modeling, scenario planning, or optimization methods applied to capacity or supply decisions
Familiarity with data center power delivery, cooling, or site selection constraints in a hyperscale environment
Experience partnering with finance organizations on capital planning or capital expenditure forecasting
Experience with hardware supply chain planning, including supplier lead times, constraints, and procurement cycles
